summary.headline: Nava Q1 FY27 consolidated total income hit an all-time quarterly high of INR1,269 crore; Phase 2 thermal (MEL) slips to Q2 FY28-29 commissioning.
summary.overview: Management reported record consolidated total income of INR1,269 crore for Q1 FY27, with standalone total income at a record INR689 crore, helped by lower coal and manufacturing costs and dividend income from Nava Global. The 300 MW MEL plant ran at an 89.3% PLF. Phase 2 thermal commissioning has been pushed by a couple of months to around July 2027 (Q2 FY28, per management wording) due to logistics delays on critical equipment linked to the geopolitical conflict. A 100 MW solar project is slated for commissioning by end-September 2026. Management did not disclose consolidated profit or margin figures in the call.

segments.name: Energy (MEL 300 MW, Zambia)
segments.commentary: MEL 300 MW plant operated at 89.3% PLF. Zambia energy sustainable EBITDA margin cited at 45-50%, with recent decline attributed to lower reversal of ECL credit.

segments.name: Metals (manganese/ferro-alloys)
segments.commentary: Nikhil Devineni said quarterly sales dipped as the Orissa unit was under long-term maintenance shutdown; it resumed operations on 1 August 2026. Spot pricing up about 5-10% QoQ; around 70% of production committed under long-term or quarterly contracts.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.commentary: Consolidated EBITDA expected at 35-40% of segment EBITDA after intersegment eliminations. Zambia reported on 100% consolidation basis.

guidance_outlook: MEL Phase 2 thermal (2 units): full commissioning by Q2 FY28 (around July 2027); first unit slightly earlier; no material capex impact stated.
MEL Phase 2 expected revenue about INR200 million; project cost INR400 million, funded INR300 million debt and INR100 million equity.
100 MW solar project to be commissioned by end-September 2026; management expects it to open a new niche and further investment in solar.
Sugar plant (Zambia) commissioning targeted Q4 FY28, with revenue of INR55-60 million per annum.
Expected return on equity on the new 300 MW phase about 15%; no tax holiday currently for Phase 2, company pursuing one with government.
Metals margins expected to be stable or slightly higher; no downward trend seen until end of FY27.
Dividend policy of at least 30% of PAT (stated as Nava Global policy).
capex_capacity: MEL Phase 2 thermal: two units, full commissioning by Q2 FY28 (around July 2027) after logistics delays on critical materials and equipment; earlier target was Jan-Feb 2027.
100 MW solar project: commissioning by end-September 2026.
Zambia projects in implementation: thermal energy, renewable energy, avocado and sugar; some expected to yield revenue shortly.
Exploration: lithium (Zambia) slowed by elections; manganese concession of 360 sq km with detailed exploration on only 2 sq km, now moving to exploitation licence.
Management said Phase 2 Maamba commissioning is later than originally envisaged but no material impact on capex.
Maamba bi-annual maintenance shutdown scheduled in the current quarter.
demand_pricing: Metals spot price improved about 5-10% QoQ; around 70% of output contracted under long-term or quarterly contracts.
Management described metals as volume-driven rather than margin-driven; sales were lower in Q1 due to Orissa shutdown.
Zambia operations reported as fine with no power disruptions from West Asia crisis.
Management flagged significant challenges from geopolitical and supply-chain disruption and said remedial actions are being taken.

qa_highlights.question: Expected commissioning and revenue from thermal Phase 2 expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Full commissioning of both units by Q2 FY28 (around July 2027); Phase 2 revenue about INR200 million; margins not disclosed, with tariff described as attractive.

qa_highlights.question: Why are land assets carried at historical cost and what is their current value?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Accounting Standards allow historical cost; management has engaged a third party to study current asset values and options, and declined to give a number.

qa_highlights.question: Is funding available for new power projects (solar, wind, SMR) and is Zambia spin-off planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all current projects are adequately funded from equity and cash, with no need to sell assets. Nava Limited is 100% ultimate owner of Nava Global; Zambia assets were always under Nava Global.

qa_highlights.question: Why was consolidated deferred tax high and will it persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Deferred tax INR40 crore this quarter vs INR163 crore prior quarter, linked to Kwacha-USD rate; CFO said it may reverse depending on exchange rate on reporting date.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Zambia energy EBITDA margin declined and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower reversal of ECL credit; sustainable EBITDA margin around 45-50%.

qa_highlights.question: How is consolidated EBITDA derived from segment EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Intersegment transfer pricing (power-metals and coal from mines) is eliminated; consolidated EBITDA is around 35-40% of segment EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Is Phase 2 finance cost capitalised?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, finance cost on Phase 2 is capitalised, as required under Ind AS and IFRS.

qa_highlights.question: Why is metals sales flat and what is the margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Orissa unit shutdown reduced Q1 sales; unit resumed on 1 August 2026. Margins expected stable or slightly up through FY27.

risks_watch: Phase 2 thermal commissioning slipped again risk: Q2 FY28 target depends on delayed critical equipment shipments amid geopolitical conflict.
Deferred tax volatility tied to Kwacha-USD exchange rate; Q1 charge INR40 crore vs INR163 crore prior quarter.
Phase 2 has no tax holiday yet; company is pursuing one from government.
Land and real-estate asset values carried at historical cost; third-party valuation study pending with no timeline given.
Lithium exploration slowed by Zambia elections; manganese exploitation licence conversion pending.
Zambia Ivory Coast manganese alloy plant depends on a government-held mine JV approval that is still pending.
Margins not disclosed for MEL Phase 2 and metals margins only qualitatively guided.
summary.management_tone: Confident on headline numbers and funding, but evasive on specifics: declined to give a margin for Phase 2, a land valuation, or a timeline for manganese exploitation. Delays were attributed to external factors.
key_quotes: We have started the year on a strong note with consolidated total income reaching an all -time quarterly high of INR1,269 crores.
We don't need to sell the assets in distress or to basically generate cash at this point.
Right now, I don't think we want to talk about the margins.
